study.title: Acupuncture modulates the frequency-specific functional connectivity density in primary dysmenorrhea
study.randomization: Patients with PDM were randomized to VA and SA groups using a random number table
study.population: Women aged 18–30 years, right-handed, with primary dysmenorrhea
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) Women aged 18–30 years, right-handed; (2) those with PDM diagnosed using the Society of Obstetricians and Gynecologists of Canada's diagnostic criteria; (3) patients with regular menstrual cycle (27–32 days); (4) patients with at least 1-year history of PDM; and (5) no exogenous hormones or centrally acting medicine in the previous 6 months; (6) pain assessed by visual analog scale (VAS) averaged over four points in the last 3 months
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) diagnosis of secondary dysmenorrhea due to organic pathology by ultrasound or gynecological examination; (2) suffering from other chronic pain conditions; (3) severe basic disorders; (4) mental illness, or with severe psychiatric disorders; (5) pregnant, preparing for pregnancy or breastfeeding; (6) treated with acupuncture in the past 3 months or have been taking analgesic medication for a long period; (7) contraindications to MRI examination; and (8) severe cranial anatomical asymmetry or well-defined lesions found on MRI scans

arms.dropouts: 2 excluded from data processing for incomplete fMRI data, 1 excluded for head movement exceeding 1.5 mm

extraction_notes.note: Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported in this study. No relevant instruments or data were provided.
Adverse events were not reported anywhere in the manuscript.
Trial registration number is not reported in the manuscript.

Supplementary Figures 1, 2, and 3, and Supplementary Table 1 are referenced but not provided in the PDF. Supplementary Figure 1 contains the acupoint locations; Supplementary Figure 2 contains the participant flow chart; Supplementary Figure 3 and Supplementary Table 1 contain RMANOVA between-group comparison results with coordinates. The coordinates for between-group RMANOVA contrasts (C17, C18) could not be extracted as they are in the supplementary table.

The sham acupuncture procedure details are sparse. Needle penetration depth for sham is not reported; it is only stated that the SA acupoints were at 'the midpoint between SP6 and the Bladder meridian without known clinical effects.' Whether needles actually penetrated the skin in SA is not explicitly stated.

Table 2 lists 'Post > Pre' for Full low frequency VA with a dash (–), meaning no significant increase; only decreases were found at FLF for VA. This was preserved as an empty coordinates_or_clusters array in C02.

The paper states in Figure 3 caption 'The gFCD changes at Slow-4 band of the right S2 in patients with PDM was positively correlated with the change in VAS scores (r = –0.587, p = 0.006).' The text body states 'r = 0.587, p = 0.006' and labels the correlation 'positive', but the figure caption reports 'r = –0.587'. This is an internal inconsistency. Both values are reported as stated; the abstract states 'S2 at the Slow-4 band was positively correlated with VAS scores.' C20 preserves the positive direction per main text while noting the figure caption discrepancy.

The paper states n_total_randomized = 47 (47 completed baseline observations and fMRI scans), but 58 were recruited. 41 out of 47 completed 3-month treatment (22 VA, 19 SA). After exclusions, 20 VA and 14 SA were analyzed. The total analyzed is 34.
No deqi quantitative scale (e.g., MASS, Southampton Needle Sensation Questionnaire) was administered. Only the requirement for deqi in VA is described narratively.

The paper states scans were conducted 'within 72 h of menstruation, with a total of two scans (including three scans in the baseline period and three scans in the treatment period).' This appears internally inconsistent (two scans vs. three scans); likely means three scan sessions at baseline averaged and three scan sessions at post-treatment averaged, yielding two time points for analysis. Exact number of individual scans per participant is unclear.
The paper references a FOV for fMRI of 240 mm × 240 mm and flip angle = 90°, but does not report slice gap or number of volumes per session explicitly beyond '250 scan time points' total.

Figure 1 and Figure 2 show brain renderings of gFCD distributions. The primary coordinate data are in Tables 2 and 3 which were fully extracted. No additional coordinates were readable exclusively from the figures.

No independent sample t-test p-value is provided for post-treatment values of VAS, CMSS-s, etc. between groups; only the post-pre change T and p values are given in Table 1 for between-group comparisons.
